# Section 020: Secure Service-To-Service Communication

Makes the reader able to encrypt and authenticate traffic between workloads and allow only named callers, with Istio (primary, full depth) and Linkerd (compact). It follows access control because mesh identity is built from the service accounts set up there, and it comes before admission control because the policy engines later govern mesh objects.

**Curriculum item covered:** Configuring Secure Service-to-Service Communication

---

## What You Will Master

- Name the SPIFFE identity a workload presents from its namespace and service account
- Switch a namespace from PERMISSIVE to STRICT mTLS with PeerAuthentication and prove plain-text traffic is refused
- Write an AuthorizationPolicy that allows only the shuttle service account to call scout with GET
- Read a 403 RBAC access denied response and name the policy and rule that decided it
- Order ALLOW, DENY and CUSTOM policies and predict the result when several match
- Find the workload whose sidecar is missing and so breaks STRICT mTLS
- Inject the Linkerd proxy into a namespace and confirm with linkerd viz edges or linkerd check that connections use mTLS
- Name the Linkerd identity of a workload from its service account
- Write a Server and an AuthorizationPolicy with a MeshTLSAuthentication that let only shuttle call scout
- Set a default inbound policy (all-unauthenticated, all-authenticated, deny) and predict who is refused
- Map each Linkerd resource to the Istio resource that does the same job

## The Learning Path

### 1. Require Mutual TLS And Authorize Callers With Istio
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Require Mutual TLS And Authorize Callers With Istio](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-020/module-01/playground` — kind cluster with Istio 1.31.1 installed by istioctl (minimal or default profile, sidecar mode), no Linkerd. Namespace `starfleet` labelled for sidecar injection with `scout`, `probe` and `shuttle` (each own service account). Namespace `outpost` without injection, running `drifter` (the plain-text caller). Mesh starts in the default PERMISSIVE mode with no PeerAuthentication and no AuthorizationPolicy, so drifter can still reach scout at the start.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS021.git -c sections/section-020/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Require Mutual TLS And Authorize Callers With Linkerd
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Require Mutual TLS And Authorize Callers With Linkerd](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-020/module-02/playground` — kind cluster with Linkerd edge-26.10.1 (CRDs, control plane and the viz extension) installed by the linkerd CLI, no Istio. Namespace `starfleet` annotated for proxy injection with `scout`, `probe` and `shuttle`; namespace `outpost` without injection running `drifter`. Default inbound policy left at all-unauthenticated, no Server or AuthorizationPolicy yet, so drifter can reach scout at the start.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS021.git -c sections/section-020/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Secure Service-To-Service Communication Capstone — `sections/section-020/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS021.git -c sections/section-020/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** On an Istio mesh, the `starfleet` namespace must accept only mTLS traffic, `scout` must answer only GET requests from `shuttle`, and `probe` must be reachable only from inside `starfleet`. One workload starts without a sidecar and must be fixed so it keeps working under STRICT. The grader sends requests from shuttle, drifter and a plain-text client and checks each answer.
